remaining_concerns: The affected health-plan benefits support use case remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
There is no admissible evidence of reviewed and approved risk acceptance addressing that exposed weakness.
The policy states rollout controls mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or reviewed risk acceptance exists; neither condition is shown.
No admissible evidence shows the final launch record or model card already contains the required explicit disclosure.
Disclosure may be required, but the record does not show that disclosure alone is sufficient for certification while the exposed weakness remains unresolved.
final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and expressly conceded the key missing predicates: no approved risk acceptance, no proof of final disclosure language, and continued exposure of the affected use case. The response narrows the claim and correctly rejects the overbroad argument that rollout controls alone cure the weakness, but that is a reinterpretation of the same record, not new evidence. Under the policy text, rollout controls and monitoring can mitigate this weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or reviewed risk acceptance explains why exposure is acceptable. The current record shows neither. A caveated certification theory based on future or intended disclosure is therefore still missing an unresolved compliance predicate, not merely a presentation caveat. That keeps the claim noncompliant on the present evidentiary record.
